title: EU AI Act Article 10 — Data and Data Governance Requirements for High-Risk AI Systems
context: 2026-09-01 05:15 BST EAT cycle — answer-first seed covering the EU AI Act's data governance mandate for high-risk AI: training, validation, and testing data quality, bias detection, and documentation obligations that took effect August 2026.
body: EU AI Act Article 10 imposes mandatory data governance requirements on all high-risk AI systems placed on the EU market or put into service within the Union. It is one of the most operationally demanding articles in the Regulation because it governs the raw material of every AI system: the data. The core requirements are: (a) Training, validation, and testing datasets must be subject to appropriate data governance and management practices covering design choices, data collection, origin, preparation, assumptions, and examination of possible biases. (b) Datasets must be relevant, sufficiently representative, appropriately vetted for errors, and as complete as possible in view of the intended purpose. (c) Where strictly necessary for bias monitoring and correction, providers may process special categories of personal data under Art 9(1) GDPR — but subject to safeguards including pseudonymisation, technical controls preventing re-use, and a data protection impact assessment. (d) The governance practices must include an examination of possible biases likely to affect health and safety, fundamental rights, or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law. (e) Appropriate measures to detect, prevent, and mitigate biases must be implemented. The practical implications are significant: every high-risk AI provider must now maintain a data governance dossier that documents sourcing decisions, representativeness analysis, bias examination methodology, and remediation steps. This is auditable. At the Council of AI Measurement Board, the Governance axis (237 items) and Privacy axis (32 items) both intersect with Art 10 compliance: the Governance bank tests whether a model can correctly classify data-governance scenarios, while the Privacy bank tests PII leakage and special-category-data handling. Article 10 came into application on 2 August 2026, and the AI Office has signalled data governance as a priority enforcement area for Q4 2026 market surveillance.
